chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Arriving in New York: the Cotton Club and the theater circuit
summary: They opened at the Capitol Theater then the Cotton Club with Stormy Weather revue, broadcasting nightly. The band also played fourteen weeks of New York theaters by day, sleeping on cots between shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So we came into New York and -- opened at the Capital Theater. And during that week -- we were going to follow that week and go into the Cotton Club the next week. Well, during that week they took me up to the Cotton Club to see the show. And I had never seen anything like that, you know, out West and all that. So I was very happy and thrilled to be here.

So now payday came at the theater. Well, the guy comes around with the pay envelopes and I opened my envelope and there was $100.00, you know. So I go to Cab and I said, "well, I owe you for what I drew, the money I drew and for the Arrang -- (Unintelligible), you know. He said, 'Just forget about it. You don't owe me anything, you know.'"
So now that very next week we opened the Cotton Club.
And they were doing -- I think they were doing -- starting the Stormy Weather Review there with Ethel Waters. And this was a gas.

I mean, we were broadcasting every night. And now in those days we used to do 14 weeks right here in New York of theater during the day, while playing at the Cotton Club. You know, we'd play the Harlem Opera House and then we'd play the theater down here on 14th Street.
The Academy of Music. And we'd play like the Capital Theater and we played the Paradise Theater in the Bronx and we'd play the Jamaica Theater in Jamaica. And all the circuits around here.
Would the Flabush go in there too? and the Winsor in the Bronx?

Right. And we played these the other weeks weeks, one week, one week after that we was doing the Cotton Club. So we'd be so tired, you know, because we would play the theater and we'd get to the Cotton Club in time to do the first show, which is 12:00 o'clock at night. And they'd have a band there playing until we got there and then we'd do the first show at 12:00 and the second show at 2:00 and we'd get through about 4:00. Then we'd have to be at the theater the next day, maybe at 11:00 for the first show. But we used to hang out because Harlem was running 24 hours a day. No one ever went to bed, only slept between shows on cots, you know. So this was the way that routine was.
